overview: The Callaway Community Redevelopment Agency is a dependent district and blended component unit of the City of Callaway, with the City Commission serving as its board. It was created by City Ordinance 829 (audits give May 8, 2007) and adopted its redevelopment plan by Resolution 07-13 in 2007. The district covers roughly 1,400 acres in the commercial core along Tyndall Parkway (US-98) and Highway 22. Tax increment was small until about FY2021, then rose quickly to more than $1.1 million in FY2025, while spending lagged far behind budget. Fund balance therefore grew to about $2.25 million by the end of FY2025.

It takes in the Tyndall Parkway (US-98) and Highway 22 commercial corridors. Bay County GIS polygon area works out to about 1,366 acres.

controversies.summary: Year after year, CRA spending ran far below budget. FY2025 capital outlay was about $316K against a $3.14M budget, so the restricted fund balance built up to about $2.25M. Audits blamed delayed property rehab and spillway projects and business grants with no applicants.

data_gaps: Callaway's CRA annual reports (for example the 2023 annual report), CRA agendas and minutes, and budget resolutions (CRA Res 2021-01) are on cityofcallaway.com, but that site couldn't be read by our tools. These would name vendors and projects.
No vendor-level payments were found. Check the CRA board agenda packets in the city AgendaCenter.

No CRA audit for FY2020 or earlier could be found on the Auditor General's site. Tax increment history for FY2016-FY2020 is unknown apart from FY2021's $54,221, taken from the FY2022 audit comparison.
The 2007 Redevelopment Plan PDF on the city site returned an error, so planned project costs and the sunset date were not captured.

The Tyndall Parkway median beautification (2019-2020, $500K, Lawnscapes Inc.) and the Cherry Street rehab ($5M) were reported as state/FDOT funded with no CRA funding mentioned, so they are excluded. Confirm whether any CRA money went in.
There is no confirmed CRA tie to the Callaway Arts & Conference Center.
Adopted CRA budget totals for FY2024-FY2027 were not found.

overview: The Springfield Community Redevelopment Agency was created by Resolution/Ordinance 07-05 on March 30, 2007. It is a component unit of the City of Springfield, and the City Commission sits as its board. The base taxable value was about $67.6 million; by February 2025 the area was valued at about $118.4 million. For several years the CRA collected TIF but spent nothing, and auditors found the City had not transferred its own share of the increment for FY2022-2024. Recent budgets put the built-up reserves toward park and sidewalk projects (Springfield Gardens Walking Park, Nature Park, Buddy McLemore Park, Carrie Bell Shaw Park, and 2nd/3rd Street sidewalks).

controversies.summary: The FY2024 audit reported a material weakness: the City had not calculated or transferred its required share of the tax increment to the CRA for FY2022-2024, an estimated $291,027. The auditor attributed this to a lack of understanding of the requirement.

The FY2025 audit repeated the finding on late City transfers, estimating the cumulative underfunding at $526,519. A catch-up transfer was made in September 2025. The audit also found the CRA had not sent its budgets to Bay County within the 10 days required by s.163.387(6), F.S.
The 2024 annual report said none of the redevelopment plan's goals had yet been met and no projects had been completed. Reserves were only being built up at that point.

data_gaps: Several Springfield PDFs are scans with no text: the FY24-25 budget, Res 2025-02 and Res 2025-03, and the minutes for Nov 2024, May 2025 and Sept 2025. Their line items and vendor awards have not been transcribed yet.
The audit for FY2023 and earlier and TIF history for 2016-2022 were not found. Check the Florida Auditor General special district e-file or City of Springfield ACFRs.
No vendor or contractor names were found for the park and sidewalk projects. The amounts listed are budget appropriations, not paid invoices.
No CRA spending on the Transmitter Rd or 15th St corridor was documented.
Exact park coordinates (Nature Park, Carrie Bell Shaw Park, Buddy McLemore Park) are not geocoded.

overview: The Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of Parker was established May 25, 2004, by City Council Resolution 2004-05-350. It is a dependent district governed by the City Council. For most of its history it had no positive tax increment: it received $0 TIF in FY2023 and ran a tiny budget for audit costs. Increment collection finally began in FY2024 ($247,539) and grew in FY2025 ($393,198), with spending so far limited to reimbursing the City.

districts.name: Parker Community Redevelopment Area
districts.boundary_description: Two pieces along the US-98 (Tyndall Pkwy / Hwy 98) corridor through Parker. The northern section runs roughly from 30.127 to 30.146 N, between about -85.591 and -85.615. A smaller southern section near the St. Andrew Bay shoreline runs roughly from 30.105 to 30.125 N. Acreage is derived from the Bay County GIS polygon area (25.84M sq ft).
